section_summary: This section documents U.S. concern in 1936 that Japanese research vessels and floating canneries might begin taking salmon in international waters near Bristol Bay. Coast Guard reports, diplomatic correspondence, private letters, and press clippings track Japanese vessels, discuss the three-mile limit, and weigh possible effects on Alaskan fisheries. Later documents describe proposals for joint research and Japan’s reluctance to negotiate fishing restrictions.

subfiles.title: Coast Guard cover letter on Japanese vessels
subfiles.about: Forwards a Bering Sea Patrol dispatch on Japanese vessels near Alaska.
subfiles.summary: Transmits the patrol dispatch for the commissioner’s information.

subfiles.title: Bering Sea Patrol dispatch on Japanese vessels
subfiles.about: Reports Hakuyo Maru’s movements and the locations and apparent operations of three other Japanese ships.
subfiles.summary: Lists Hakuyo Maru, Chichibu Maru, Toten Maru, and a presumed supply ship.

subfiles.title: Commerce request for surveillance of Tenyo Maru
subfiles.about: Requests discreet Coast Guard observation of a Japanese fisheries investigation near Bristol Bay.
subfiles.summary: Commerce fears the Tenyo Maru expedition may identify offshore salmon fishing grounds for future floating canneries and asks for close observation and a report.

subfiles.title: Japanese Floaters Start for Bering Sea Fishery
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese crab vessels leaving Hakodate and Commissioner Bell’s assessment of their licenses.
subfiles.summary: Bell says their crab and fish-meal licenses give no immediate reason to expect salmon fishing.

subfiles.title: Bureau instructions to observe Tenyo Maru
subfiles.about: Relays Grew’s report of the Tenyo Maru expedition and requests confidential sightings.
subfiles.summary: Bureau vessels are asked to report the location and activities of Tenyo Maru and its auxiliary.

subfiles.title: Bell’s response to Pacific Fisherman
subfiles.about: Discusses Japanese salmon fishing rights, conservation concerns, and plans to monitor Tenyo Maru.
subfiles.summary: The Bureau acknowledges Gray’s information, explains the difficulty of restricting fishing on the high seas without agreement, and describes plans to observe Japanese research. It cites earlier American offshore salmon catches and encloses a clipping about Japanese pearlers in Australia.

subfiles.title: Japanese Pearlers Annoy Australia
subfiles.about: Describes allegations that Japanese pearlers violated Australian territorial and customs rules.
subfiles.summary: Reports vessel beaching, water collection, and pearl fishing near the three-mile limit.

subfiles.title: Gray forwards Japanese Diet petition
subfiles.about: Quotes a petition urging Japan to develop open-sea salmon fishing in the northeastern Pacific.
subfiles.summary: Gray cites a private correspondent’s account of Diet members pressing for mother-ship salmon operations near Alaska.

subfiles.title: Gray’s warning about Bristol Bay salmon
subfiles.about: Urges surveillance and American research into offshore Bristol Bay salmon fishing.
subfiles.summary: Gray suspects Japan’s scientific expedition is testing whether salmon can be caught beyond the three-mile limit. He advocates observation, diplomatic preparation, and an American study of offshore fishing methods.

subfiles.title: Memorandum forwarding Allen’s confidential letter
subfiles.from: Department of State Legal Adviser’s office
subfiles.to: Department of State Far Eastern Affairs officers
subfiles.about: Forwards Edward W. Allen’s letter for confidential filing.
subfiles.summary: Notes that Allen has been told his letter reached the appropriate State Department officers.

subfiles.title: Allen on Japanese salmon-fishing petition
subfiles.about: Warns of a Japanese petition seeking salmon fishing and floating canneries on the Alaska side of Bering Sea.
subfiles.summary: Allen relays confidential information about the Diet petition, a Japanese research vessel, and a Hakodate fisheries scholar visiting Bristol Bay. He links Japan’s interest to declining Siberian fisheries and fears destructive offshore salmon fishing.

subfiles.title: Hull forwards Allen information to Commerce
subfiles.about: Sends confidential extracts from Allen’s letter about Japanese fishing near Alaska.
subfiles.summary: Asks Commerce to preserve the writer’s requested confidentiality.

subfiles.title: Extract from Allen’s letter
subfiles.about: Summarizes the petition and Allen’s fears about Japanese floating canneries near Bristol Bay.
subfiles.summary: Allen predicts trouble if Japanese mother ships fish for salmon beyond the three-mile limit.

subfiles.title: Coast Guard report on Chichibu Maru’s nets
subfiles.about: Quotes a patrol report describing Chichibu Maru’s gill nets and salmon catch.
subfiles.summary: Reports two-mile surface nets, pink salmon, and fur seals feeding from the nets.

subfiles.title: Bureau inquiry into Chichibu Maru
subfiles.about: Seeks corroboration of a patrol report that Chichibu Maru was fishing for salmon.
subfiles.summary: The reported salmon gill nets conflict with the Bureau’s information on Japanese vessel licenses.

subfiles.title: Duplicate Coast Guard cover letter
subfiles.about: Forwards the Bering Sea Patrol dispatch on Japanese vessels.
subfiles.summary: Copy of the cover letter on page 481.

subfiles.title: Duplicate Bering Sea Patrol dispatch
subfiles.about: Reports Hakuyo Maru’s route and nearby Japanese fishing and support vessels.
subfiles.summary: Copy of the dispatch on page 482.

subfiles.title: Modern Research Ship Seeks New Grounds for Japanese Fisheries
subfiles.about: Describes a Japanese research ship equipped for fishing, canning, refrigeration, and laboratory work.
subfiles.summary: The article presents its modern equipment as part of Japan’s search for new fishing grounds.

subfiles.title: Bureau reply to Farish
subfiles.about: Acknowledges confidential information on possible Japanese salmon operations near Alaska.
subfiles.summary: The Bureau says State and Commerce are monitoring the issue and explains the difficulty of restricting high-seas fishing.

subfiles.title: Farish forwards Canadian Legation memorandum
subfiles.about: Forwards H. Sawa’s confidential memorandum and corrects its Gulf of Anadyr geography.
subfiles.summary: Farish notes that Anadyr lies far from the Gulf of Alaska.

subfiles.title: Salmon Pack Prospects in Kamchatka
subfiles.about: Estimates Japanese salmon packs and reports an exploratory floating cannery sent toward the Gulf of Anadyr.
subfiles.summary: Sawa compares expected and earlier Kamchatka catches and reports that a Nichiro subsidiary sent a vessel to investigate new salmon grounds.

subfiles.title: Commerce reply to Hull on Alaskan fisheries
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Allen’s information and describes Coast Guard surveillance plans.
subfiles.summary: Commerce fears that Japanese floating canneries taking salmon would injure American packers and expects patrol observations to guide policy.

subfiles.title: Grew reports Japanese account of Chichibu Maru
subfiles.about: Relays Japan’s claim that Chichibu Maru lacked a Bristol Bay salmon license.
subfiles.summary: The Foreign Office says the ship abandoned its Anadyr fishing trip and became a transport vessel.

subfiles.title: Hull forwards Chichibu Maru telegram to Navy
subfiles.about: Sends Grew’s telegram concerning the vessel reported fishing near Alaska.
subfiles.summary: Transmits the ambassador’s account for Navy information.

subfiles.title: Hull forwards Chichibu Maru telegram to Commerce
subfiles.about: Sends Commerce Grew’s response to the Coast Guard report on Chichibu Maru.
subfiles.summary: Links the embassy inquiry to Waesche’s earlier report.

subfiles.title: Navy acknowledgment
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of Grew’s telegram about Chichibu Maru.
subfiles.summary: Thanks State for forwarding the vessel report.

subfiles.title: Grew despatch on Bristol Bay and fur seals
subfiles.about: Encloses an embassy conversation on Japanese fishing in Bristol Bay and possible Fur Seal Treaty revision.
subfiles.summary: Grew notes that Okamoto raised treaty revision during discussion of salmon fishing, possibly linking the two issues.

subfiles.title: Neville–Okamoto conversation
subfiles.about: Records Japan’s response to the Chichibu Maru report and discussion of salmon licenses and fur seals.
subfiles.summary: Okamoto says the Foreign Office has no information about Chichibu Maru but will investigate. He describes Japanese reluctance to license Bristol Bay salmon fishing, pending research into profitability, and mentions possible future changes to the Fur Seal Treaty.

subfiles.title: State forwards Grew’s fisheries despatch
subfiles.about: Sends Grew’s despatch and flags Okamoto’s reference to the Fur Seal Treaty.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the Tokyo conversation to Commerce.

subfiles.title: Jones warns of risks to fisheries loans
subfiles.about: Raises concern that Japanese offshore salmon fishing could harm U.S. fisheries and outstanding federal loans.
subfiles.summary: Jones cites Japanese research funding and possible damage to salmon runs and companies indebted to the Reconstruction Finance Corporation.

subfiles.title: Japanese Eye North American Fisheries
subfiles.about: Reviews Japan’s research plans, Diet petition, and reported pearling disputes in Australian waters.
subfiles.summary: The article describes the Tenyo Maru investigation and a petition for Japanese mother-ship salmon fishing near Alaska. It also recounts allegations that Japanese pearlers disregarded Australian rules.

subfiles.title: Hull replies to Jones
subfiles.about: Explains prior U.S. diplomatic efforts concerning Japanese salmon fishing near Bristol Bay.
subfiles.summary: Hull recounts informal Japanese assurances against private Bristol Bay salmon licenses, U.S. knowledge of Japanese research visits, and Japan’s decision to defer treaty talks until its investigations finish. He assures Jones that State and Commerce are following the threat to Alaska’s salmon industry.

subfiles.title: Bell acknowledges Kanda report
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Freeman’s account of Seiji Kanda’s fisheries proposals at Yosemite.
subfiles.summary: Bell plans further consideration of Japanese activity in Bristol Bay’s high-seas waters.

subfiles.title: Allen forwards Freeman’s letter
subfiles.about: Sends Freeman’s letter concerning Kanda’s Yosemite presentation.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the enclosure at Freeman’s request.

subfiles.title: Freeman reports Kanda’s Yosemite proposals
subfiles.about: Describes Kanda’s proposals for joint North Pacific salmon research and discussion of Asian fisheries.
subfiles.summary: Kanda proposes U.S.–Japanese research in Bristol Bay and the Aleutians as a basis for treaty talks, plus study of Russian–Japanese fisheries. The private meeting reaches no conclusion and refers possible research to an Institute committee.

subfiles.title: Fisheries Service Bulletin
subfiles.about: Reports staff retirements and U.S. Senate ratification of the Fraser River sockeye salmon treaty.
subfiles.summary: Bulletin page covering two retirements and the treaty.

subfiles.title: Patrol extract on Kanda’s trap study
subfiles.about: Records Seiji Kanda’s visit to salmon traps near Funter Bay.
subfiles.summary: The Widgeon carried Kanda to inspect pile and floating traps.

subfiles.title: Japan Studying Fishing, Bristol Bay Region, Now
subfiles.about: Describes Hakuyo Maru’s Bristol Bay research and warns of competition in canned-fish exports.
subfiles.summary: Reports student training, experimental equipment, and research sampling aboard the ship.

subfiles.title: File note on Kanda in Bristol Bay
subfiles.about: Notes the Scoter’s transport of Kanda among Bristol Bay fishing communities.
subfiles.summary: Kanda traveled from Naknek to Egegik and Ugashik and back, June 25–28.

subfiles.title: High Japanese to Visit North
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese consul Isaku Okamoto’s arrival in Ketchikan.
subfiles.summary: Okamoto is traveling to Alaskan cities and Fairbanks.

subfiles.title: Studies Alaska Fishing Industry
subfiles.about: Reports Kanda’s visit and call for a bilateral salmon-study committee.
subfiles.summary: Kanda discusses salmon movements in the Bering Sea and North Pacific.

subfiles.title: Japanese Commence Investigation of Bristol Bay Salmon Fishery
subfiles.about: Details Japanese research ships, Hakuyo Maru’s experimental catches, and Kanda’s fisheries tour.
subfiles.summary: The article describes Tenyo Maru’s research assignment, crab factory ships, and Hakuyo Maru’s Bristol Bay salmon experiments, including gill-net catches canned aboard. It also reports Kanda’s interest in regulation, salmon tagging, and international research.

subfiles.title: Bureau acknowledges Tenyo Maru sighting
subfiles.about: Acknowledges a Coast Guard report locating Tenyo Maru in Bristol Bay.
subfiles.summary: Notes that no fishing was observed.

subfiles.title: Coast Guard cover letter on Tenyo Maru
subfiles.about: Forwards a confidential patrol dispatch on Tenyo Maru.
subfiles.summary: Identifies Daphne and Alert as Coast Guard vessels.

subfiles.title: Bering Sea Patrol dispatch locating Tenyo Maru
subfiles.about: Reports Tenyo Maru anchored with a trawler in Bristol Bay on July 20.
subfiles.summary: Alert saw no nets or fishing operations.

subfiles.title: Bureau acknowledges Hakuyo Maru report
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the Cyane’s report and Hakuyo Maru cruise schedule.
subfiles.summary: Adds the information to the Bureau’s files.

subfiles.title: Cyane report on Hakuyo Maru and endorsements
subfiles.from: J. A. Dirks; endorsed by R. W. Dempwolf and M. J. Ryan
subfiles.to: Commander, Bering Sea Patrol Force; forwarded to Coast Guard Headquarters
subfiles.about: Describes Hakuyo Maru’s Kiska visit, shipboard equipment, personnel, and route toward Bristol Bay.
subfiles.summary: Cyane officers boarded Hakuyo Maru, counted its crew and students, inspected its laboratory and small cannery, and spoke with Captain Nakagawa. Cyane then trailed the ship after it left Kiska. Later endorsements forwarded the report through Coast Guard channels.

subfiles.title: Kanda calls for international salmon study
subfiles.about: Quotes Kanda supporting a U.S.–Japanese committee on salmon movements.
subfiles.summary: Brief report of Kanda’s remarks during an Anchorage stop.

subfiles.title: Japanese Official Visits
subfiles.about: Reports Consul Okamoto’s return through Cordova after an Alaska trip.
subfiles.summary: Notes his consular appointment and visit to Mr. Mitamura.

subfiles.title: Bureau acknowledges Alert’s Tenyo Maru report
subfiles.about: Acknowledges a confidential report on Tenyo Maru.
subfiles.summary: Promises to retain the report as confidential.

subfiles.title: Coast Guard transmits Alert’s report
subfiles.about: Forwards Alert’s confidential report on Tenyo Maru.
subfiles.summary: Requests confidential handling of the enclosure.

subfiles.title: Alert’s observations of Tenyo Maru
subfiles.about: Describes Tenyo Maru and its companion trawler at anchor in Bristol Bay.
subfiles.summary: Alert saw no fishing while present; the report details the ship’s appearance and extensive radio and navigational equipment.

subfiles.title: Crawford forwards Alaska Weekly editorial
subfiles.about: Sends an editorial and expresses concern about Japanese floating-cannery training.
subfiles.summary: Crawford says his visit to Hakuyo Maru supports the editorial’s account and seeks comments.

subfiles.title: A Serious Situation
subfiles.about: Warns that Japanese offshore salmon fishing could threaten Alaska’s industry and export markets.
subfiles.summary: The editorial describes Hakuyo Maru’s training and research, then urges American action and an international agreement.

subfiles.title: Rawls acknowledges Crawford’s editorial
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the Alaska Weekly editorial and forwards it within Commerce.
subfiles.summary: Sends the material to Charles E. Jackson for information.

subfiles.title: Bell explains Bristol Bay jurisdiction
subfiles.about: Explains that no decision specifically declares Bristol Bay waters beyond three miles extraterritorial.
subfiles.summary: Bell cites the general U.S. three-mile jurisdiction rule. He supports publication of factual information about Japanese salmon fishing and its effects on American industries.

subfiles.title: Gray asks for Bristol Bay legal authority
subfiles.about: Requests the published legal basis for treating parts of Bristol Bay as extraterritorial waters.
subfiles.summary: Gray asks for references he can consult in Seattle.

subfiles.title: Dickover on Japan’s refusal of fisheries agreement
subfiles.about: Reports a Japanese newspaper account of official views on salmon fishing restrictions near Canada and Alaska.
subfiles.summary: Dickover says the account suggests Japan still opposes negotiations on a restrictive convention. The translated summary claims Japan has barred salmon floating canneries from Canadian and Alaskan waters, while arguing that Japan should reject a proposed international prohibition or restriction.
